s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive, painless jaw swelling with multilocular radiolucent lesions
salient_findings: Bilateral, symmetrical enlargement of the mandible and maxilla
Well-defined, multilocular radiolucent areas on panoramic radiography
Expansile, multilocular lesions with thinning of cortical plates on computed tomography
key_facts: Two-year-old boy
Progressive, bilateral, painless swelling of the jaws
Symmetrical enlargement of the mandible and maxilla
Intact, bluish-gray oral mucosa
Normal vital signs
No lymphadenopathy
Unremarkable routine hematologic tests
Panoramic radiography showed well-defined, multilocular radiolucent areas
Computed tomography showed bilateral, expansile, multilocular lesions
Thinning of the cortical plates of the maxilla and mandible
Mild anterior displacement of an unerupted first molar
No cortical breaches or soft-tissue extension

shortlist.label: Cherubism
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral, painless jaw swelling with multilocular radiolucent lesions in a young child

shortlist.label: Central giant cell granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Multilocular radiolucent lesions in the jaws with cortical thinning

shortlist.label: Brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism
shortlist.why_kept: Radiolucent jaw lesions, although less likely given normal hematologic tests

shortlist.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Expansile, multilocular lesions in the jaws with thinning of cortical plates

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Ground-glass appearance on radiographs not mentioned, but still a consideration

shortlist.label: Ossifying fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Well-defined, radiolucent jaw lesions with possible cortical thinning

shortlist.label: Juvenile aggressive ossifying fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive variant of ossifying fibroma, possible given patient's age

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Less likely given bilateral, symmetrical involvement and lack of systemic symptoms

raw.rationale: The condition presents with symmetrical, bilateral, painless swelling of the jaws, which is characteristic of Cherubism, particularly in a two-year-old boy. The presence of well-defined, multilocular radiolucent areas and expansile lesions with thinning of the cortical plates also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Central giant cell granuloma
rejected.why: Typically presents with unilateral jaw swelling and more aggressive features

rejected.label: Brown tumor of hyperparathyroidism
rejected.why: Associated with hyperparathyroidism, which is not indicated by the normal hematologic tests

rejected.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
rejected.why: Usually presents with a rapid onset of symptoms and more pronounced cortical expansion

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Typically presents with ground-glass appearance on radiographs and is not usually bilateral and symmetrical

rejected.label: Ossifying fibroma
rejected.why: Usually presents as a well-defined, unilocular radiolucency, not multilocular

rejected.label: Juvenile aggressive ossifying fibroma
rejected.why: Presents with more aggressive features and rapid growth

rejected.label: Eosinophilic granuloma
rejected.why: Part of Langerhans cell histiocytosis, which typically presents with systemic symptoms and lymphadenopathy
